samples.summary: Non-envelope failures now discard the upstream message, conflicting with the CLI design doc's error matrix
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1024-1042 (§10 Error Matrix) specifies `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM | (original message preserved)` and `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`. `forwardUpstreamError` collapses every non-envelope failure (including a Nest 404 body carrying `message: 'Document not found'`, and any 5xx) to `throw new Error('HTTP <status>')`, which `outputError` reports as `{error:{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}}` with exit code 1. The framework body's `message` — the only human/agent-usable detail — is dropped, and no status→code mapping (NOT_FOUND / UNAUTHORIZED / SYSTEM) or exit-code-2 path is introduced. The helper is exactly the layer where that mapping belongs, and the new end-to-end test at packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:175 locks in the `{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}` shape as intended behavior.

samples.summary: Sibling call site still forwards non-envelope bodies verbatim — the same defect this change fixes, left inconsistent
samples.evidence: `files download` does `io.stderr(JSON.stringify(res.data ?? { error: { code: 'HTTP_ERROR' } }, null, 2))`, so an Express/Nest body (`{message, error:'Not Found', statusCode}`) is still emitted verbatim, producing exactly the `error.code === undefined` output the new `isErrorEnvelope` guard exists to prevent. `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41` likewise pulls `error.message` out of an unvalidated body. If the goal is 'a consumer can always branch on error.code', these paths should either reuse `forwardUpstreamError` or be explicitly out of scope.

samples.summary: Envelope shape re-declared instead of reusing the existing `ApiError` type
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:26` already defines the canonical envelope `ApiError { error: { code: string; message: string; command?: string } }`. `isErrorEnvelope` declares an inline structural duplicate (`{ error: { code: string; message?: string } }`), so the documented shape now has two definitions that can drift. The predicate could be `body is ApiError`.

samples.summary: HTTP-response handling placed in the output/formatting layer
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` takes an HTTP `{status, data}` shape and decides transport-error policy, but lives in `src/output/formatter.ts`, whose other exports (`format`, `output`, `outputError`) only serialize values. The response/error-policy concern sits with `src/client/` (where `ApiResponse`/`ApiError` and `sessionExpiredBody` already live); putting it there would also let `files/download.ts` and `sheets-export.ts` reuse it without importing the output layer.

samples.summary: No design-doc row records the new 'upstream body is not the documented envelope' behavior
samples.evidence: The change establishes a new documented contract — only bodies matching the envelope are forwarded verbatim, everything else becomes `{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP <status>'}` — but neither docs/design/cli.md §10 (Error Matrix) nor packages/cli/README.md's Errors section (line 116-122) mentions it. This is a behavior/contract note rather than an architecture change, so it likely folds into the existing cli.md matrix rather than a new doc.

finding.summary: Non-envelope failures now discard the upstream message, conflicting with the CLI design doc's error matrix
finding.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1024-1042 (§10 Error Matrix) specifies `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM | (original message preserved)` and `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`. `forwardUpstreamError` collapses every non-envelope failure (including a Nest 404 body carrying `message: 'Document not found'`, and any 5xx) to `throw new Error('HTTP <status>')`, which `outputError` reports as `{error:{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}}` with exit code 1. The framework body's `message` — the only human/agent-usable detail — is dropped, and no status→code mapping (NOT_FOUND / UNAUTHORIZED / SYSTEM) or exit-code-2 path is introduced. The helper is exactly the layer where that mapping belongs, and the new end-to-end test at packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:175 locks in the `{code:'ERROR',message:'HTTP 404'}` shape as intended behavior.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out against the repository. formatter.ts:104-109 forwards only bodies passing the structural isErrorEnvelope test (76-85) and throws `new Error('HTTP <status>')` for all other failure bodies, discarding the upstream `message`. outputError (57-63) then emits code 'ERROR' (errorCode, 41-47, since a bare Error has no `code`) and hard-codes process.exitCode = 1, so no exit-2 or NOT_FOUND/UNAUTHORIZED/SYSTEM path exists. The cited design-doc rows are verbatim present at docs/design/cli.md:1038-1039 ("Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED", "Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM | (original message preserved)"), reinforced by cli.md:780-782. The behavior is reachable from six live call sites (docs.ts:197,249; slides.ts:154,197; notes.ts:148,195), each wrapped in a try/catch routing to outputError (docs.ts:209-211), and a repo-wide grep found no status-to-code mapping or exitCode=2 anywhere in packages/cli, so no upstream guard makes it unreachable — http-client.ts:156-164 only produces a SESSION_EXPIRED envelope. The new test at packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:167-172 asserts {code:'ERROR', message:'HTTP 404'} with exit 1 for all six commands, locking in the divergence. Conflict with the canonical CLI design doc's error matrix is squarely spec-conformance (design-fit lane), so no refutation ground applies.
